A useful converter model must cover several time scales at once: nanosecond
switch edges, a microsecond switching period, and millisecond startup. This
project also mixes a discrete event switch with a nonlinear diode and energy
storage in the LC filter.

## Build a nonideal power stage

The switch has finite on-resistance. The catch diode includes series resistance,
junction capacitance, and reverse breakdown. The inductor and capacitor include
winding resistance, ESR, and leakage rather than behaving as ideal components.

```{julia}
@circuit ProjectBuck(; input_voltage=12V, switching_frequency=250kHz,
        duty_cycle=0.42, inductance=47μH, capacitance=100μF,
        load=10Ω) begin
    gnd = ground()
    vin = node(); gate = node(); switching = node(); output = node()

    Input = voltage_source(vin, gnd; dc=input_voltage)
    Gate = voltage_source(gate, gnd; dc=0V,
        waveform=Pulse(low=0V, high=5V, frequency=switching_frequency,
            duty_cycle=duty_cycle, rise=5ns, fall=5ns))
    HighSide = analog_switch(vin, switching, gate, gnd;
        model=EventSwitch(threshold=2.5V, ron=80mΩ, roff=1TΩ))
    Catch = diode(gnd, switching;
        model=JunctionDiode(saturation_current=20nA, ideality=1.15,
            series_resistance=40mΩ, junction_capacitance=80pF,
            breakdown_voltage=40V))
    Filter = inductor(switching, output; value=inductance,
        winding_resistance=120mΩ)
    Output = capacitor(output, gnd; value=capacitance, esr=35mΩ,
        leakage_resistance=1MΩ)
    Load = resistor(output, gnd; value=load)

    observe(voltage(gate), voltage(switching), voltage(output),
        current(Filter), current(HighSide), current(Catch), power(Load))
end

converter = ProjectBuck()
check(converter)
```

`event_mode=:exact` makes the integrator land on switch transitions. The circuit
starts with discharged energy-storage elements, so the result includes the
full startup rather than assuming an already-established periodic orbit.

```{julia}
startup = transient(converter, 0s => 2ms; initial=:discharged,
    event_mode=:exact, max_step=100ns, saveat=1μs, reltol=1e-5)

settled = startup.axis .>= 1.5ms
average_output = mean(voltage(startup, :output)[settled])
output_ripple = peak_to_peak(voltage(:output); window=1.5ms => 2ms)(startup)
average_load_power = mean(power(startup, :Load)[settled])

(average_output, output_ripple, average_load_power,
    converged=startup.stats[:converged])
```

## Inspect startup and switching ripple

The upper panel establishes the slow startup envelope. The lower panel zooms
into the final 25 switching periods and keeps voltage and current on separate
axes with their correct units.

```{julia}
figure = Figure(size=(1050, 820))
traceplot(figure[1, 1], startup; signals=:output, color="#0072B2")
traceplot(figure[2, 1], startup; signals=[:output, current(:Filter)],
    interval=1.9ms => 2ms)
Label(figure[0, 1], "Buck converter startup and settled ripple"; fontsize=21)
figure
```

The ideal estimate is $D V_{in}=5.04$ V. The difference from the measured mean
is the combined effect of diode drop, switch resistance, winding resistance,
and ripple—precisely why the nonideal model is worth simulating.

::: {.callout-note}
This is an asynchronous buck converter: when the high-side switch opens, the
catch diode carries the inductor current. A synchronous design would replace
that diode with a second controlled switch and explicit dead time.
:::
